```{r Step 0: data ingestion, include=TRUE}
ces2024 <- read_dta(here("00_rawdata", "CCES24_Common_OUTPUT_vv_topost_final.dta"))
ces2022 <- read_dta(here("00_rawdata", "CCES22_Common_OUTPUT_vv_topost.dta"))
ces2020 <- read_dta(here("00_rawdata", "CES20_Common_OUTPUT_vv.dta"))
ces2018 <- read_dta(here("00_rawdata", "cces18_common_vv.dta"))
ces2016 <- read_dta (here("00_rawdata", "CCES16_Common_OUTPUT_Feb2018_VV.dta" ))
```

#2024 Analysis
```{r Step 1: Create Index of Life Changes for Each Wave, include=FALSE}
#2024 Wave 
life_event_vars_2024 <- c("CC24_305_1", "CC24_305_2", "CC24_305_4", 
                     "CC24_305_5", "CC24_305_6", "CC24_305_9", "CC24_305_10", "CC24_305_13")

# Create the index by counting how many variables equal 1 (Yes)
ces2024$life_events_index_2024 <- rowSums(ces2024[life_event_vars_2024] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate how many valid responses each person has (not missing)
ces2024$valid_responses <- rowSums(!is.na(ces2024[life_event_vars_2024]))

# Alternative index that accounts for missing data
# (sets to NA if person answered none of the questions)
ces2024$life_events_index_alt_2024 <- ifelse(ces2024$valid_responses > 0, 
                                       ces2024$life_events_index, 
                                       NA)

# Check the distribution of your new index
table(ces2024$life_events_index_2024, useNA = "always")

# Start regression modeling with index regressed on partisan strength
# First, examine the partisan identification variable
table(ces2024$CC24_pid7, useNA = "always")

# Create partisan strength variable
# This measures distance from the center (4 = Independent)
# Higher values = stronger partisanship (closer to 1 or 7)
ces2024$partisan_strength <- abs(ces2024$CC24_pid7 - 4)

# Check the distribution of partisan strength
table(ces2024$partisan_strength, useNA = "always")

# Run the regression: life events predicting partisan strength
model_partisan_2024 <- lm(partisan_strength ~ life_events_index_2024, data = ces2024)

# View the results
summary(model_partisan_2024)

# Get confidence intervals
confint(model_partisan_2024)

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship
plot(ces2024$life_events_index_2024, ces2024$partisan_strength, 
     xlab = "Life Events Index", 
     ylab = "Partisan Strength (Distance from Independent)",
     main = "Life Events vs Partisan Strength (2024)")

# Add the regression line
abline(model_partisan_2024, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Calculate correlation
cor(ces2024$life_events_index_2024, ces2024$partisan_strength, use = "complete.obs")


#Redo model but add in covariates
# First, examine the race variable
table(ces2024$race_24, useNA = "always")

# Convert race to a factor with meaningful labels
ces2024$race_factor <- factor(ces2024$race,
                             levels = 1:8,
                             labels = c("White", "Black", "Hispanic", "Asian", 
                                       "Native American", "Middle Eastern", 
                                       "Two or more races", "Other"))


#Next is gender
ces2024$gender_factor <- factor(ces2024$gender4,
                             levels = 1:4,
                             labels = c("Man", "Woman", "Non-Binary", "Other"))

#Next is education
ces2024$educ_factor <- factor(ces2024$educ,
                              levels = 1:6,
                              labels = c("Less than HS", "HS Grad", "Some College", "2-Year Grad", "4-Year Grad", "Post-grad"))

#Next is income
ces2024$income_factor <- factor(ces2024$faminc_new,
                               levels = c(1:17),
                               labels = c(
                                 "<10k", "10-19k", "20-29k", "30-39k", "40–49k", "50–59k", "60–69k",
                                 "70–79k", "80–99k", "100–119k", "120–149k", "150–199k", "200-249k",                                     "250-349k", "350-499k", "500k+", "Prefer Not to Say"
                               ))

#Next is views on National Economy
ces2024$econ_view_factor <- factor(ces2024$CC24_302,
                                   levels = 1:5,
                                   labels = c("Much Better", "Somewhat Better", "About the Same", "Somewhat Worse", "Much Worse"))

# Age is up next 
# Create age variable (assuming survey was conducted in 2024)
ces2024$age <- 2024 - ces2024$birthyr_post

# Check the age distribution
summary(ces2024$age)
hist(ces2024$age, main = "Age Distribution", xlab = "Age")

# Finally, we'll impute region
ces2024$region_factor <- factor(ces2024$region,
                                levels = 1:4,
                                labels = c("Northeast", "Midwest", "South", "West"))

# Run the regression with covariates
model_partisan_full_2024 <- lm(partisan_strength ~ life_events_index_2024 + race_factor + gender_factor + educ_factor + income_factor + econ_view_factor + age + region_factor, 
                              data = ces2024)

summary(model_partisan_full_2024)


model_partisan_full_2024_2 <- lm(partisan_strength ~ life_events_index_2024 + race_factor + gender_factor + educ_factor + income_factor + age + region_factor, 
                              data = ces2024)

summary(model_partisan_full_2024_2)

# Next step is to make a new index using emergency expense responses

```

# 2022 Wave
```{r Step 1}
# 2022 Wave
# Create a vector of the variable names for 2022
life_event_vars_2022 <- c("CC22_305_1", "CC22_305_2", "CC22_305_4", 
                          "CC22_305_5", "CC22_305_6", "CC22_305_9", "CC22_305_10", "CC22_305_13")

# Create the index by counting how many variables equal 1 (Yes)
ces2022$life_events_index_2022 <- rowSums(ces2022[life_event_vars_2022] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate how many valid responses each person has (not missing)
ces2022$valid_responses_2022 <- rowSums(!is.na(ces2022[life_event_vars_2022]))

# Alternative index that accounts for missing data
# (sets to NA if person answered none of the questions)
```
